dimensions.name: Requirements and scope
dimensions.description: Clarifies what is limited, per what key, and what accuracy and availability mean for the business.

levels.1: Repeats the prompt without defining the limit key or rule shape.
levels.2: Defines request limits but ignores bursts, overrides, or multi-region consistency.
levels.3: Separates functional and non-functional requirements and states the key, window, and consistency assumptions.
levels.4: Also quantifies acceptable over-admission, explains fail-open versus fail-closed per endpoint, and names the customer-facing contract.

dimensions.name: API and contract
dimensions.description: Defines the rejection response, quota headers, rule configuration, and override interfaces.

levels.1: Returns an error but no status code or headers.
levels.2: Uses 429 but omits Retry-After, remaining quota, or reset time.
levels.3: Defines 429 with Retry-After and quota headers, plus a way to configure rules and overrides.
levels.4: Also covers idempotent rule changes, per-plan defaults, allowlists, and how clients should back off.

dimensions.name: Counters and storage
dimensions.description: Chooses keys, counter representations, expiry, and a store that matches the access pattern.

levels.1: No concrete counter or key model.
levels.2: Stores a simple count without atomicity, TTL, or a plan for hot keys.
levels.3: Defines keys, atomic updates, expiry, and a store such as Redis with a clear eviction policy.
levels.4: Also explains sharding, hot-key mitigation, clock assumptions, and how counters survive a store restart.

dimensions.name: Placement and architecture
dimensions.description: Places the limiter in the request path and balances local enforcement with a shared store.

levels.1: Adds a remote limiter call to every request with no local path.
levels.2: Describes a limiter service but not how gateways and services share state.
levels.3: Shows gateway middleware, a local fast path, a shared counter store, and a config distribution path.
levels.4: Also explains how the two tiers reconcile, how rules roll out safely, and why the boundaries sit where they do.

dimensions.name: Scale and performance
dimensions.description: Sizes the check path and shows how it stays fast under peak traffic.

levels.2: Repeats the numbers without estimating QPS, latency, or store load.
levels.3: Estimates per-tier QPS and describes pipelining, local caching, and horizontal scaling.
levels.4: Also quantifies p99 overhead, hot-key behavior, Redis cluster sizing, and the cost of the chosen accuracy.

dimensions.name: Trade-offs
dimensions.description: Compares algorithms and enforcement models and defends the chosen balance.

levels.2: Names an algorithm without connecting it to the traffic shape.
levels.3: Compares at least two algorithms or enforcement models, such as fixed window vs token bucket or local vs distributed.
levels.4: Also explains when the chosen option is wrong, how over-admission is bounded, and what would trigger a redesign.

dimensions.name: Failure modes and operations
dimensions.description: Covers store outages, clock issues, bad rules, and the metrics that reveal them.

levels.1: Assumes the counter store never fails.
levels.2: Mentions fail-open or fail-closed without a recovery path.
levels.3: Identifies the main failure modes and the metrics or alerts that detect them.
levels.4: Also covers degraded-mode limits, hot-key overload, bad-rule rollback, and a runbook for disabling the limiter safely.
